title: Blood in the Head, a Cut in the Cord

questions.stem: A blow to the temple, a lucid interval, then a crash. The blood is shaped like:
questions.explanation: Epidural blood makes a lens and often has a lucid interval.

questions.stem: A crescent of blood after a fall in an older adult is typically from:

options.text: A cut in half the cord
A first thought of amyloid in a deep nucleus

questions.explanation: A crescent is subdural blood from bridging veins.

questions.stem: A ring-enhancing brain lesion that may be an abscess. First move?

options.text: Do not start with a spinal tap. Image and protect.
Treat it as a simple migraine

questions.explanation: A lumbar puncture can herniate a tight brain.

questions.stem: A deep bleed in the basal ganglia of an adult with long-standing high pressure is most often related to:
questions.explanation: Deep bleeds often follow chronic high pressure. Lobar bleeds in older adults raise concern for amyloid.

questions.stem: A lobar surface bleed in an older adult raises concern for:

options.text: A purely epidural lens from a temple blow

questions.explanation: Lobar hemorrhage and amyloid angiopathy go together in older adults.

questions.stem: If half the cord is cut, pain and temperature are typically lost:

options.text: On the same side as the cut
On the opposite side, because those fibers already crossed

questions.explanation: Pain and temperature have already crossed. Weakness and position sense stay on the same side.

questions.stem: A small pupil, a droopy lid, and a dry face on one side describe:

options.text: A typical central forehead-sparing picture only

questions.explanation: Horner syndrome is a sympathetic cut.

questions.stem: A facial palsy that includes the forehead is typically:

options.text: Always a central lesion that spares the forehead

questions.explanation: Bell palsy includes the forehead. A typical central lesion spares it.

options.text: Arterial, lens-shaped, and can crash fast

questions.explanation: Epidural: lens, often a lucid interval, arterial.

options.text: Epidural blood is typically a lens.
Subdural blood is typically a crescent from bridging veins.
A suspected brain abscess should start with a lumbar puncture.
Half-cord injury has weakness on the same side and pain on the opposite side.

questions.explanation: Do not start with a spinal tap when a ring-enhancing abscess is the concern.
